questions.answer: Draw the force vectors one after another so that the head of each vector meets the tail of the next. The third vector returns to the starting point, making a closed triangle, so the resultant force is zero.
accepted_alternatives: Accept an equivalent statement that all three vectors form a closed head-to-tail loop with no resultant.
questions.tolerance: Both the head-to-tail arrangement and closure as the equilibrium test are required.

Selects C: density is mass per unit volume

option_feedback.A: Mass divided by area is not density because the material volume is missing.
option_feedback.B: This reverses the density ratio; density places mass in the numerator.
option_feedback.C: Correct. Density is mass per unit volume.
option_feedback.D: Weight is a force and depends on gravitational field strength; density uses mass.

questions.unit_policy: The unit kg m^-3 is included in every option.

marking_points.text: Selects D: 2.70 g cm^-3 equals 2700 kg m^-3

option_feedback.A: This converts grams to kilograms but does not account for the cubic-centimetre denominator.
option_feedback.B: The numerical value does not stay unchanged because both the mass and cubic volume units change.
option_feedback.C: This uses a factor of 100, but 1 g cm^-3 equals 1000 kg m^-3.
option_feedback.D: Correct. Multiply a density in g cm^-3 by 1000 to obtain kg m^-3.

marking_points.text: Selects A: at equal mass, doubling density halves volume

option_feedback.A: Correct. Since V = m/rho and mass is fixed, volume is inversely proportional to density.
option_feedback.B: Equal mass does not give equal volume when the densities differ.
option_feedback.C: This treats volume as directly proportional to density instead of inversely proportional at fixed mass.
option_feedback.D: Doubling density changes the fixed-mass volume by a factor of two, not four.

questions.answer: The sphere volume is 2.68083 x 10^-4 m^3. Its mass is 2.091 kg and its weight is 20.5 N. The three force vectors form a closed triangle; the angled cord force has vertical component equal to the weight, so T sin 60.0 degrees = 20.5 N and T = 23.7 N.
questions.unit_policy: Use m^3, N and N as required; the force triangle must carry directions or labels.

parts.answer: Vertical equilibrium gives T sin 60.0 degrees = W = 20.513 N. Therefore T = 20.513 / sin 60.0 degrees = 23.7 N.
accepted_alternatives: Accept an equivalent sine-rule calculation from the correct closed force triangle.
